html:
The flight of the Circassians, a mostly Muslim people of the northwest Caucasus, into the Ottoman Empire after Russia completed its conquest of their homeland in 1864.

The Russo-Circassian War had lasted decades. At its end the Russian army drove most of the people of Circassia out of their mountains to the Black Sea coast. Hundreds of thousands were shipped across to Ottoman ports such as Trabzon and Samsun. Many died of hunger and disease on the shore, in crowded boats and in the camps where they landed. Many Circassians and some historians call the whole process a genocide. The European side of the story, the expulsion from the Caucasus, is on the chart too.

The Ottoman state settled the refugees across Anatolia, in the Balkans and in Syria and Palestine, often on the frontier. Circassian villages took root in the Golan and around Amman, which grew from their settlement in the 1870s. In Jordan Circassians later served in the royal guard. Most Circassians today live in Turkey and the Middle East, not in the Caucasus.
sum: The flight of the Circassians, a mostly Muslim people of the northwest Caucasus, into the Ottoman Empire after Russia completed its conquest of their homeland in 1864.
